jobs.description:
About Us

Snappy Shopper is the UK’s fastest‑growing quick commerce (Q‑commerce) platform powering rapid grocery delivery from local convenience stores. We enable independent retailers and major partners, including SPAR, Nisa, Premier, Co‑op and others, to digitally transform their business by offering same‑day and rapid delivery of food, drink and everyday essentials within as little as 30‑60 minutes. Customers on our platform typically spend significantly more online than in‑store, helping retailers grow revenue and deepen community engagement.

We’re more than a delivery app, we’re a technology partner for local high streets, providing tools for digital sales, marketing solutions, and integrations that help retailers compete with larger online players.

At Snappy Shopper, we’re committed toinnovation, retail empowerment and community impact, helping stores thrive digitally, offering exceptional local convenience to customers, and shaping the future of on‑demand retail in the UK.

Our location

We are a UK company with colleagues across the country and offices in Dundee and Edinburgh. This is a fully remote role, with occasional opportunities to connect with colleagues in person.

About the team

You'll join our Android team, working closely with Product, Engineering and customer-facing colleagues across the business.

Our Android estate is broader than a single consumer app.

Snappy Shopper is our consumer ordering app, built in Kotlin with Jetpack Compose, Coroutines and Flow.

Order Manager receives orders in-store and supports picking, substitutions, refunds, receipt printing and driver assignment.

Snappy Pickeris used by store and warehouse teams to scan and pick products and manage gaps and substitutions.

Order Manager and Snappy Picker also mean working with older Kotlin, RxJava2 and XML codebases running on rugged hardware in thousands of stores, often over patchy connectivity and in sessions lasting all day. Here, reliability matters more than pixel polish.

About the role

As an experienced Android Developer, you’ll combine strong hands-on Android development with the independent technical judgement and ownership.

Day-to-day, you will:

  • Design, build and maintain Android features across Snappy Shopper, Order Manager and Snappy Picker.

  • Work with other Android developers and wider stakeholders to turn business requirements into clear technical approaches and deliverables.

  • Make sound technical decisions, considering architecture, reliability, maintainability and the wider impact of your implementation.

  • Take ownership of the quality and completeness of your solutions before they reach review.

  • Review other developers’ code and contribute constructively to technical discussions.

  • Troubleshoot existing Kotlin and legacy Java code and help resolve complex production issues.

  • Work pragmatically, recognising when something needs solving properly now and when improvement is better left for another day.

To be successful, you'll have:

We’re looking for someone with strong level of Android capability rather than a checklist of every technology we use.

You’ll bring strong modern Kotlin experience, including reviewing other developers’ Kotlin and contributing meaningfully to PR discussions.

You’ll also have:

  • Production experience with Jetpack Compose.

  • Strong experience with Coroutines and Flow.

  • Hilt, Dagger 2 or Koin experience, with a good understanding of dependency scoping.

  • Experience working with multi-module Clean Architecture, where architecture and code-quality standards are enforced through tooling and CI.

  • A strong unit-testing habit, using technologies such as JUnit and MockK/Mockito.

  • Experience with collaborative development, version control and code review.

  • Experience working within an Agile/Scrum environment.

Our apps currently ship at minSdk 24–26 and targetSdk 35–36.

We’d also like you to have done at least one of these:

  • Worked with RxJava2, including good disposal discipline.

  • Shipped a hardware integration using a vendor SDK, AIDL service, Bluetooth device or partner-app Intent.

  • Shipped realtime functionality using WebSockets, including fallback and dead-connection handling.

  • Worked with custom Dagger scopes or subcomponents with explicit teardown.

Exposure to XML/ViewBinding, Room, Crashlytics, payment SDKs, Firebase Remote Config, WorkManager, Bluetooth printing or similar technologies is useful, but isn't essential.

And there are things we don't expect you to know before you arrive. You'll learn our store domain and the hardware behind it, including Sunmi POS devices and scanners, PayPoint terminals, Zebra scanners and Bluetooth label printers.

Who you are

  • Community: You collaborate well, share knowledge and help others reach better technical solutions.

  • Be Snappy: You work at pace, adapt to changing priorities and take ownership of delivery.

  • Breaking Barriers:You use sound technical judgement to solve difficult problems and aren't afraid to constructively challenge an approach when there's a better one.

  • Craic on: You communicate clearly, build trusted relationships and enjoy working with technical and non-technical colleagues.

What’s in it for you

Joining Snappy as an Android Developer means working on more than another consumer mobile app.

You'll work across modern Compose development and established applications that sit at the heart of day-to-day store operations. You'll encounter interesting challenges around reliability, hardware, payments, realtime communication and applications operating in imperfect real-world conditions.

You'll have autonomy in how you solve problems, the opportunity to influence our Android engineering approach and a team that values good judgement as much as technical knowledge.

We offer a competitive salary, flexible remote working and ongoing opportunities for learning and development.

Applying

We want our recruitment process to give you (and us) a proper opportunity to understand whether the role is the right fit.

Following an initial application review, selected candidates will have an introductory conversation with our Engineering team to discuss your experience, the role and Snappy's Android environment.

Candidates progressing from there will take part in practical technical sessions involving different Android development scenarios and live coding exercises, giving us the opportunity to understand how you approach problems, write and work with code, make technical decisions and respond as requirements or constraints evolve.

We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds and are committed to inclusive recruitment.

Please note that due to the volume of applications we receive, we’re only able to contact candidates who are selected to progress to the next stage.

SQL (Clickhouse), Metabase, Python, Jupyter Hub, GitHub.

jobs.description:
Veeam is the Data and AI Trust Company, specializing in helping organizations ensure their data and AI are fully understood, secured, and resilient to enable the acceleration of safe AI at scale. As the market leader in both data resilience and data security posture management, Veeam is built for the convergence of identity, data, security, and AI risk. Headquartered in Seattle with offices in more than 30 countries, Veeam protects over 550,000 customers worldwide, who trust Veeam to keep their businesses running. Join us as we go fearlessly forward together, growing, learning, and making a real impact for some of the world’s biggest brands.

About the Role

The ideal candidate is naturally collaborative, articulate, highly organized, and passionate about helping customers achieve measurable business outcomes. Success in this role requires a combination of strong technical expertise, business acumen, executive communication skills, and a customer-first mindset.

As a Senior Customer Success Engineer (CSE), you serve as the customer's trusted technical advisor and primary technical owner, guiding customers through customer activation, adoption, optimization, expansion, and renewal. You will develop and execute tailored Customer Success Plans, align technical adoption to business objectives, strengthen customers' resilience posture, and proactively identify opportunities and risks throughout the customer lifecycle. Success in this role requires the ability to understand each customer's unique goals, challenges, and environment, then translate those insights into a personalized strategy that drives measurable outcomes.

You will leverage deep expertise across the Veeam portfolio to help customers maximize value, improve recovery readiness, advance data resilience maturity, and achieve their desired outcomes while partnering closely with Sales, Customer Success leadership, and other Veeam teams.

What You’ll Do

  • Own the technical customer relationship for a portfolio of strategic Enterprise and Commercial Named accounts, serving as a trusted advisor throughout the customer lifecycle.
  • Build, maintain, and advance tailored Customer Success Plans aligned to each customer's business objectives, technical priorities, desired outcomes, and success criteria.
  • Guide customer activation, drive adoption and optimization, and help customers realize measurable value from their investment across the Veeam portfolio.
  • Conduct health assessments, architecture reviews, protection strategy evaluations, and solution adoption planning across the Veeam portfolio.
  • Assess recovery readiness, identify opportunities to improve resilience, and provide strategic recommendations aligned to customer objectives.
  • Facilitate recovery simulations, resilience reviews, and best-practice discussions to strengthen customer confidence and preparedness.
  • Monitor customer health signals and adoption trends to proactively identify risk, develop mitigation plans, and improve retention outcomes.
  • Partner with Account Executives and Customer Success leadership to identify expansion opportunities through customer outcomes, product adoption, and demonstrated business value.
  • Develop executive-ready business reviews, resilience reports, and success updates for technical and executive stakeholders, including Director, Vice President, Chief Information Security Officer, and Chief Information Officer audiences.
  • Coordinate and advocate across Veeam teams to remove blockers, accelerate outcomes, and ensure a consistent customer experience.
  • Deliver strategic guidance around data protection, recovery, cyber resilience, cloud adoption, operational efficiency, and portfolio optimization.
  • Maintain a high-touch engagement model supporting a limited portfolio of high-value customers, typically accounts with more than $200,000 in annual recurring revenue.
  • Own the technical success plan and adoption roadmap; provide technical insight, customer outcome validation, and risk assessments that support renewal and expansion strategy in partnership with Sales and Customer Success leadership. 

What You’ll Bring

  • 5+ years of experience in customer-facing technical roles such as Customer Success Engineering, Technical Account Management, Solutions Engineering, Consulting, Professional Services, or similar positions focused on data protection and recovery technologies.
  • Strong technical expertise across backup and recovery, virtualization, operating systems, storage, cloud platforms, cybersecurity, and automation technologies.
  • Experience designing and validating protection strategies, recovery preparedness programs, modernization initiatives, and migration projects.
  • Proven ability to translate customer business objectives into technical roadmaps, adoption strategies, and measurable outcomes.
  • Strong executive communication skills with experience presenting technical, operational, and risk-based recommendations to senior stakeholders.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple strategic customer relationships while driving measurable success outcomes.
  • Proven consultative mindset with the ability to adapt engagement strategies and success plans to varying customer priorities, technical environments, and business challenges.
  • Excellent collaboration, communication, stakeholder management, and consultative problem-solving skills.
  • Experience conducting technical assessments, health reviews, architecture discussions, and executive business reviews.
  • VMCE certification required or obtained within an agreed-upon timeframe following hire. 

Bonus Skills

  • Advanced knowledge of the Veeam portfolio and data resilience technologies, including backup, recovery, cyber resilience, cloud data protection, and related solutions.
  • AWS Solutions Architect (Associate or Professional), Microsoft Azure Administrator Associate, Microsoft Azure Solutions Architect Expert, or equivalent cloud platform certifications.
  • Security-focused certifications such as Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP), Certified Cloud Security Professional (CCSP), CompTIA Security+, or equivalent.
  • Infrastructure and enterprise platform certifications such as VMware Certified Professional (VCP), Red Hat Certified Engineer (RHCE), Microsoft Windows Server certifications, Cisco Certified Network Associate (CCNA), or equivalent.
  • Experience working with enterprise-scale environments, cyber resilience initiatives, ransomware recovery planning, disaster recovery programs, or information security frameworks.
  • Experience advising executive and technical stakeholders on resilience, security, cloud modernization, or infrastructure transformation initiatives.

What you'll get

  • Unlimited paid time off, 12 paid holidays including 4 global VeeaMe Days for self-care and 24 paid volunteer hours annually through Veeam Cares

  • Opportunities to learn and grow through on-demand libraries (LinkedIn Learning, O’Reilly), mentoring, workshops, and learning events like our annual Global Day of Learning

jobs.description:
About the Program:

Every year, we sponsor 2 remote UX apprentices from anywhere in the world to join us for 7 months, either in the fall or spring seasons or online. Our UX apprentices work through the end-to-end UX design and UX research process for a startup idea of their choice that will help them attract hiring managers in that topic space or industry.
Apprentices take our program for free and receive 1:1 mentorship throughout the 7-month program. Alumni UX apprentices go on to make between $85,000 -$130,000 in UX design, product design, UX research, or service design roles after they complete the program.
We are committed to helping women, immigrants, POC, and LGBTQ folks break into tech and land 6-figure UX jobs. We help you land 6-figure UX jobs or coach you till you get it.

Apprenticeship Requirements:

This apprenticeship program is open to new grads and UX career changers alike! Here are some apprenticeship requirements to keep in mind before applying:
Interested in creative tech career paths in UX research, UX design, product design or service design
Willing to commit 5-10 hours of work per week to complete program deliverables
Willing to attend 2-3 hour weekend lectures to learn the end-to-end design process OR willing to complete online video course modules
Open to feedback from UX mentors and demonstrates a willingness to revise design work

Apprenticeship Program Learnings:

Build digital products and services 0-1
Lead end-to-end design process for a startup idea or topic of your choice
Lead product scoping and feature scoping, as well as entire project management
Identify target market for product and position product for launch success
Develop a business model for the product or service and demonstrate how the product/service will scale as the business model scales
Lead discovery research by managing user recruitment, creating research plans, writing interview guides, leading 8-16 discovery interviews, and synthesizing interview insights
Deliver a compelling UX design and business pitch for your startup idea, showcasing both qualitative and quantitative data to justify the problem space and the solution
Tell a compelling story about users by showcasing user types, personas, stakeholder maps, journey maps, process maps, service blueprints, ideation matrixes, sketches, wireframes, UX workflows, prototypes and other visual deliverables
Lead user testing of wireframes and prototypes to improve product/service usability and constantly iterate on your startup idea
Design a unique design system for your solution from scratch, creating components, a style guide, and branding for your solution
Analyze direct and indirect competitors to clearly articulate your solution’s differentiators and why your solution is innovative and more likely to succeed over competing options
Consult with startups to create a scope of work and fulfill UX research, UX design, product design and service design work based on your scope of work.

How to Apply:

The application takes a few minutes to complete and will ask you to send in your resume. You do NOT need to have a UX resume or portfolio to apply- we consider folks who are at the very beginning of their career change, who are still exploring multiple career options.
You will receive UX tips and challenges via email to help you with your transition into UX and will be contacted by us if you are being considered for the apprentice program. Once contacted, you will go through a brief interview process before joining the cohort. Due to the large volume of applicants, we cannot contact all applicants about their application status. If you don’t hear from us about an interview within 2 months of applying, please consider your application closed. We consider applicants on a rolling basis.

jobs.excerpt: The companySmall businesses move fast.  Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight.
jobs.description:
The company

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.

Hybrid in Berlin or London

We’re looking for a Growth Product Manager

Own the systems that decide which German businesses iwoca reaches, and the journey they take from first click to submitted loan application. You’ll join a team that is still being built, with a data scientist in place and engineers being hired in parallel. A good fit if you like working from first principles, and would rather run an experiment than win an argument.

The team

The DE Acquisition Tech team builds the systems behind how German businesses discover iwoca and apply for funding: the models that decide which businesses to approach, the eligibility checks that tell a business early whether iwoca can help, and the signup flow itself. Product, analytics, data science and engineering sit in the same squad by design, so the team can go from hypothesis to shipped change without waiting on anyone else. The German marketing and sales teams depend on this work: the team’s models decide who they contact, and its journeys decide how many of those businesses convert.

The team is being built right now. It currently includes a data scientist, and we’re hiring engineers in parallel – so you would join early enough to shape how the team operates.

The role

This role sits between iwoca’s German commercial teams – marketing, sales and commercial strategy – and the technical squad that builds for them. Reporting into the Head of Direct Acquisition, you will own acquisition and activation outcomes for the German market: finding the opportunities, defining the hypotheses, and working with engineering, data, marketing and sales to build, test and iterate.

The scope is broad. We’re not looking for someone with deep expertise in every domain the team covers – spanning product development, analytics, UX and data science – but rather someone intellectually curious, and skilled at asking the right questions.

Own the funnel from first visit to application

  • Own every step of that journey, including the signup flow itself and the eligibility checks inside it.

  • Set the roadmap for acquisition and the signup journey, and decide what the squad builds next.

  • Own the scoring and segmentation that decides where marketing spends and who sales calls first.

Build with your technical squad

  • Ship lead scoring systems, eligibility checkers and signup flows with the team’s data scientist and the engineers we’re hiring.

  • Rework website content, signup flows and decisioning logic with marketing and sales, to convert more of the businesses that already reach iwoca.

  • Strip friction out of the signup journey, so that applying for funding takes minutes rather than an afternoon.

Be the first call when the numbers look wrong

  • Act as the technical partner for German marketing, sales and channel management on attribution, tracking and data pipeline problems.

  • Investigate and resolve data quality issues – broken dashboards, misattributed traffic, unexplained volume changes – often at short notice.

  • Give channel managers access to, and guidance on, the attribution logic behind their numbers.

  • Keep the tracking and attribution systems trustworthy, so every decision downstream rests on numbers the team believes.

Run the experiments that decide what ships

  • Design, run and interpret A/B tests across messaging, targeting, eligibility checks and signup flows.

  • Find opportunities from first principles, backed by data, customer research and funnel analysis.

Shape how a new team works

  • Direct the squad’s work day to day: brief the data scientist and engineers, set priorities, and turn their models into shipped products.

  • Define the priorities, roles and rituals of a team that is still being built.

  • Lead cross-functional initiatives with marketing and sales, aligning them with engineering and data on shared goals, hypotheses and success metrics.

  • Turn the commercial strategy team’s goals into testable hypotheses and briefs the squad can act on.

The requirements

Essential:

  • Experience as a product manager, growth product manager, or in a role with clear ownership of product-led growth outcomes.

  • Strong analytical capability and experience with experimentation frameworks and A/B testing tools.

  • Hands-on experience with tracking and attribution setups, such as Amplitude, GA4, GTM, server-side tagging or conversion feedback into ad platforms.

  • Able to act as the product voice on modelling work – challenging assumptions and turning model output into decisions, without building the models yourself.

  • Strong capability using AI tools, including structured prompting and iterative AI interaction to problem solve and increase productivity.

Bonus:

  • Experience in fintech, lending, B2B SaaS, or regulated products.

  • Experience working with data science teams or involvement in modelling projects.

  • Fluency in German and strong written communication skills tailored to customer-facing environments.

  • Knowledge of the German SME ecosystem or B2B financial products.

  • Experience working in or helping build newly formed teams.

The salary

We expect to pay from £60,000 - £80,000 for this role. But, we’re open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews.

The culture

At iwoca, we prioritise a culture of learning, growth, and support, and invest in the development of our team members. We value thought and skill diversity, and encourage people to explore new areas of interest, adopt better tools – including AI – and apply sound judgement so our products and decisions improve over time.

The offices

We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work:

  • Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks.

  • Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.

The benefits

  • Flexible working hours.

  • Medical insurance from Vitality, including discounted gym membership.

  • A choice between a dedicated dental plan or a health cash plan that reimburses everyday medical expenses.

  • A private GP service (separate from Vitality) for you, your partner, and your dependents.

  • 25 days’ holiday per year, an extra day off for your birthday, the option to buy or sell an additional five days of annual leave, and unlimited unpaid leave.

  • A one-month, fully paid sabbatical after four years.

  • Instant access to external counselling and therapy sessions for team members that need emotional or mental health support.

  • 3% Pension contributions on total earnings.

  • An employee equity incentive scheme.

  • Generous parental leave and a nursery tax benefit scheme to help you save money.

  • Electric car scheme and cycle to work scheme.

  • Two company retreats a year: we’ve been to France, Italy, Spain, and further afield.

And to make sure we all keep learning, we offer:

  • A learning and development budget for everyone.

  • Company-wide talks with internal and external speakers.

  • Access to learning platforms like Treehouse.

Useful links:

About Atlys

Our mission is to enable every person on Earth to travel freely.

Travel should feel exciting. Instead, too much of it is still defined by paperwork, uncertainty, and processes that were never designed for travellers.

Atlys is changing that.

We’re building an AI-first platform that removes friction and uncertainty from travel. To date, we’ve processed visas for 1M+ travellers across 127 countries. But we’re still early.

The Role

We're looking for a City Scout to help build the most reliable database of work-friendly cafes for travellers.

You'll visit cafes across your assigned city, verify information like WiFi quality, internet speed, plug points and overall work-friendliness, and submit accurate data that powers a new Atlys product. Every visit directly improves the travel experience for thousands of users.

  • Explore and discover great cafes: Visit assigned cafes across your city, experience them as a customer, and identify places that travellers would genuinely enjoy working from.

  • Enjoy exploring your city and discovering new places.

  • Have strong attention to detail and collect information accurately.

  • Are comfortable travelling independently within your city.

  • Own a smartphone and are reliable, proactive and self-driven.

We hire exceptional people for their craft, not travel enthusiasts. We solve hard problems that happen to touch global travel and government infrastructure.

What you can expect

Atlys is built by a small team with outsized ambition, high ownership, and an obsession with doing great work.

Here’s what you can expect:

  • Competitive compensation and equity so you participate in the value you help create.

  • Comprehensive health insurance covering you and your family, plus annual preventive health check-up on us.

  • Great tools to do your best work, including high-spec equipment and software.

Our values shape how we make decisions, work together and build for travelers. The bar is high, the pace is fast, and the way we work is deliberate. Read them before you apply. If this environment energizes you, you’ll probably thrive here. If it doesn’t, it’s better to know that upfront.

About Matter Health

Matter Health delivers primary and preventive healthcare directly to older adults living in public housing communities.

Total Healthcare. Where you live.

About the Role

Matter Health is seeking a Principal AI Platform Engineer to build and lead the technical foundation for our organization-wide AI capabilities. This is a senior, hands-on individual-contributor role with no direct reports. You will own the AI platform strategy, roadmap, architecture, governance, reliability, and budget while creating the environments, deployment pipelines, reusable components, connectors, and integration scaffolding that enable other teams to build and deploy AI agents and workflow automations safely.

Success in this role requires balancing enablement with protection: helping teams move quickly while establishing the standards, controls, observability, and incident-response practices needed in a regulated healthcare environment. You will partner closely with the CTO, Software Engineering, Information Security and Compliance, and clinical and operational leaders.

This is a fully remote role. Candidates located in Nashville or Memphis, Tennessee, are preferred. Occasional travel of up to 10% may be required for company meetings, team offsites, or business needs.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own the strategy, roadmap, reference architecture, and day-to-day operation of Matter Health’s enterprise AI platform.
  • Design and maintain development, testing, and production environments; deployment pipelines; reusable platform components; and secure integration patterns for AI agents and workflow automations.
  • Build connectors and integration scaffolding across enterprise systems such as EHR, CRM, ticketing, telephony, and data-warehouse platforms.
  • Evaluate and implement agent orchestration and runtime technologies, RAG and vector infrastructure, MCP or comparable integration and context-sharing frameworks, RPA, model APIs, and supporting tools.
  • Establish and enforce AI engineering standards and governance practices, including identity and access controls, PHI and regulated-data safeguards, vendor-risk review, auditability, human oversight, and safe rollback or shutdown mechanisms.
  • Define logging, monitoring, observability, reliability, and incident-response practices for production AI systems; lead root-cause reviews and continuous improvement after incidents.
  • Own the AI platform budget and vendor relationships, including usage-based cloud and model spend, vendor evaluation, contract recommendations, and platform investment decisions in partnership with the CTO.
  • Enable engineers, automation specialists, and business teams to build on the platform through clear documentation, reusable patterns, technical guidance, and hands-on problem solving.
  • Partner with technical, security, clinical, operational, data, product, and executive stakeholders to translate business needs into secure and scalable platform capabilities.
  • Measure platform adoption, reliability, business impact, and risk, and use those findings to guide roadmap priorities.

Qualifications

Required

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 10+ years of experience in software, platform, infrastructure, or related engineering roles.
  • 3+ years operating at the Staff, Principal, or Architect level with responsibility for setting technical direction across teams or an organization.
  • 2+ years personally designing, building, deploying, and operating production LLM or AI-agent systems.
  • Demonstrated ownership of an enterprise platform strategy and roadmap, including architecture, reusable tooling, deployment environments, and integration foundations.
  • Hands-on experience with AI agents, workflow automation, RAG or vector infrastructure, APIs, and enterprise integrations.
  • Experience with MCP or a comparable agent integration or context-sharing framework.
  • Experience designing governance, security, or model-risk controls for AI or other high-risk technology in a regulated environment.
  • Experience handling PHI, HIPAA-regulated data, or similarly sensitive and regulated information.
  • Experience establishing monitoring, observability, production reliability, incident response, root-cause review, and rollback or shutdown practices.
  • Direct ownership of technology budgets and vendor relationships, including usage-based cloud or model spend, vendor evaluation, and contract recommendations.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to set standards and influence technical, clinical, operational, security, and executive stakeholders without direct authority.

Preferred

  • Experience building technology platforms in healthcare or another highly regulated environment.
  • Experience with EHR, CRM, ticketing, telephony, data-warehouse, or RPA integrations.
  • Familiarity with NIST AI RMF, ONC HTI-1, CMS guidance, state AI requirements, or comparable regulatory frameworks.
  • Experience enabling distributed engineering or business teams through platform tooling, reusable components, and technical documentation.

What Success Looks Like

  • A secure, reliable, and observable AI platform is operating in production with clear standards and ownership.
  • Teams can build and deploy AI agents and automations faster by using reusable platform components, connectors, and approved patterns.
  • AI solutions meet Matter Health’s security, privacy, governance, and compliance expectations.
  • Platform reliability, usage, cost, risk, and business impact are measurable and actively managed.
  • Leaders across technology, clinical operations, and the business trust the platform and the technical guidance behind it.

Why Matter Health

At Matter Health, we believe that where you live should never determine the quality of care you receive. Every team member is vital in improving healthcare access for older adults who have historically been underserved by traditional healthcare systems.

This isn’t just a mission statement—it’s the work we do every day.

Total Healthcare. Where you live.

Working at Matter Health

Time Away

Thinking of applying? Here's the inside scoop.

Let us walk you through the next steps.

Step 1 – Complete Your Application

Fill in our application form and upload your CV. This stores your profile in our Applicant Tracking System (ATS) and places you into our active job pipelines, making it easier for us to match you with current and future opportunities.

Step 2 – The First Look (One-Way Video Interview)

This is where your application comes to life. We review your CV and video interview to get a feel for your experience, communication style, and overall fit. If we like what we see, you're on to the next step!

Why do we ask for a video?

Because a résumé can tell us what you've done, but it can't show us you. Your video is your moment to shine, and it helps us see:

  • How you communicate and connect with people.
  • How you present yourself professionally.
  • Other opportunities you might be an even better fit for (bonus surprises!).

Think of it as your personal trailer. One great video means we can pitch you for multiple roles and get you in front of the right employers, faster.

Heads up: Some clients watch your video directly, so make it one you'd be proud to have represent you. This is your highlight reel—make it count!

Step 3 – Let's Actually Talk

A Recruitment Specialist calls to chat about your experience, your availability, what you want to earn, and the role itself. Consider it a friendly vibe check.

Step 4 – The Fine Print, Made Fun

We break down what it's like working as an independent contractor—hours, pay, contract terms, the whole deal. No surprises, no fine-print sneakiness. You'll get it all in writing.

Step 5 – Matchmaking Time

Our Talent Delivery Team plays cupid, matching you to clients where you're most likely to shine. We can't promise everyone gets picked, but we're rooting for you.

Step 6 – Showtime

Got shortlisted? We'll set up your interview, prep you like a pro, and have your back the whole way—with a Reworks teammate right there facilitating.

Step 7 – The Verdict

We chase feedback the second it lands and keep you in the loop.

jobs.description:
Senior Machine Learning Engineer

Location: Montreal, Quebec, Toronto, or Ontario

About Numa

Numa is building the platform to power AI-native dealerships, rearchitecting automotive service and sales with advanced AI agents that automate customer interactions, streamline operations, and reimagine how dealerships work. Numa integrates AI into every aspect of dealership functions—from rescuing customer calls and voicemails that generate more revenue, to reducing customer resolution times that drive overall customer satisfaction (CSI), to improving dealership team productivity and accountability. Numa has raised $50 million from leading investors (Google, Threshold, Costanoa, Mitsui, and Touring Capital).

The Role

We’re hiring a Senior Machine Learning Engineer to build and ship ML/AI systems that interact with real customers thousands of times a day. Our voice agents book service appointments, rescue missed calls, and route callers through natural conversations. You’ll work across products and platforms. You’ll ship AI features including prompts, agents, tools, and production ML models, while building the evaluations and tooling that help teams ship with confidence. You’ll also contribute to our ML platform, including model serving, LLM infrastructure, and production observability. At Numa, we believe great ML is about more than building bigger models. It’s about knowing whether a change is good enough to ship. Our evaluation-first approach makes that measurable in CI and production.

What You’ll Do

  • Build conversational AI systems for phone and SMS that understand customer needs, take action, and know when to act autonomously
  • Develop tooling such as memory, knowledge graphs, and validated customization that help agents reason and adapt to dealership needs
  • Train, evaluate, and deploy ML models using Ray Serve and Dagster for prediction, classification, ranking, and capacity forecasting, and keep them healthy in production
  • Create offline and online evaluations, simulations, and CI gates that catch regressions and continuously measure quality in production
  • Implement shared evaluation, observability, and LLM tooling that helps product squads ship faster and more reliably
  • Raise the engineering bar through design and code reviews, technical writing, and mentorship
  • Work autonomously when goals are clear and help create clarity when they are not

What You Bring

  • 6+ years of software or machine learning engineering experience, with a track record of shipping ML or LLM powered systems to production
  • Strong Python and solid software engineering fundamentals; you write code others can build on, test, and trust
  • Hands-on experience building AI systems; training and deploying ML models (prediction, classification, ranking) and/or working with LLMs (prompting, tool use, agents, retrieval) with a real intuition for where they break
  • A rigorous, evaluation-first instinct, you reach for measurement to tell a real improvement from a lucky one, and a real regression from noise
  • Comfort operating with meaningful ambiguity in a product environment, and the judgment to know where to invest depth versus speed
  • Ownership and communication; you can carry a piece of work from problem framing through shipped, monitored, and improved

Nice To Have

  • Experience building or operating ML platform and tooling: evaluation frameworks, model serving, feature/prompt registries, or ML observability
  • Familiarity with our stack or its neighbors: LiveKit, Ray Serve, Dagster, Vertex AI, GCP, Kubernetes, Pulumi, or provider APIs (Anthropic, OpenAI, Deepgram, ElevenLabs)
  • Comfortable taking a model or agent from prototype to production and owning it there
  • Proficient with real-time or streaming systems: voice, telephony (SIP/WebRTC), or low-latency inference
  • Familiarity working in a startup or high-growth environment with evolving conditions

What Success Looks Like

  • Your squad ships AI features faster and with more confidence because the evals and tooling around them are solid
  • No AI change you own reaches customers without an evaluation standing behind it and regressions are caught before they ship
  • You've turned at least one hard-won squad lesson into platform leverage the rest of the team now relies on
  • Production issues in your area are understood, measured, and closed with statistical confidence that the fix actually worked
  • Other engineers are better at building AI systems because of your reviews, your writing, and how you work

Why Join Numa

  • We believe in everyone's growth
  • Be part of an industry leader named the #1 fastest-growing AI Automotive company by Inc. 5000
  • Represent category-defining AI technology that is transforming the automotive industry
  • Join a high-growth organization with significant opportunities for career advancement

Compensation & Benefits

  • Base Salary Range: $200,000 - $250,000 CAD
  • Equity Packages
  • Flexible PTO
  • Fully Covered Group Insurance

At Numa, you’ll have the chance to represent game-changing technology in an industry that’s ready for innovation. If you love being in the field, thrive on solving problems in real time, and want to make an impact at a high-growth company, we’d love to hear from you.

Job Summary

The role is responsible for analyzing customer and telecommunications data—including revenue, provisioning, ordering, billing, and contract information—to identify billing discrepancies and opportunities where the client may be under-billing its customers. The position requires a strong understanding of telecommunications products, services, ordering and provisioning processes, and billing practices, combined with strong analytical and technical skills. Identified under-billing opportunities must be analyzed, validated, and quantified, and then corrected in collaboration with the client.

Key Responsibilities

  • Perform Revenue Assurance audits for assigned telecommunications clients to identify billing inaccuracies, revenue leakage, and under-billing opportunities.

  • Analyze and reconcile multiple data sources, including customer revenue, billing, provisioning, ordering, invoice, and contract data.

  • Apply analytical techniques, including anomaly detection, trend analysis, contract analysis, order-to-bill analysis, and invoice validation, to identify potential billing discrepancies.

  • Use knowledge of telecommunications products, services, network services, ordering processes, provisioning, and billing to determine whether identified discrepancies represent actual revenue leakage or under-billing.

  • Validate identified billing issues by researching customer contracts, orders, provisioning records, invoices, and applicable billing rules.

  • Work collaboratively with client teams to correct inaccurate billing through the client's ordering and billing processes.

  • Track identified opportunities, corrections, and financial results through client portals and internal tracking dashboards.

  • Monitor the status of identified revenue assurance opportunities and follow through to ensure corrections are implemented and reflected in billing.

  • Prepare and provide analytical reports, findings, and supporting information in response to internal and client requests.

  • Meet established internal and client performance, productivity, and revenue recovery targets, and report progress against those targets.

  • Communicate findings clearly to both technical and business stakeholders, including the ability to explain the financial impact and root cause of billing discrepancies.

Required Skills & Competencies

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to identify patterns, investigate anomalies, and determine root causes.

  • Ability to work with and analyze large and complex datasets from multiple sources.

  • Strong telecommunications industry knowledge, particularly in customer ordering, provisioning, billing, contracts, and revenue processes.

  • Ability to interpret telecommunications contracts, service orders, invoices, and billing records.

  • Strong attention to detail and ability to identify discrepancies across multiple systems and data sources.

  • Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, including data analysis, reconciliation, filtering, formulas, and reporting.

  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Access and the ability to query and analyze data.

  • Proficiency with Microsoft Word and Microsoft Outlook.

  • Ability to learn and navigate client portals, billing systems, ordering systems, and internal tracking/reporting tools.

  • Ability to translate technical and analytical findings into clear business conclusions and actionable recommendations.

  • Bachelor's Degree

Compensation & Benefits

Salary Range: $50,000–$85,000 annually, with starting compensation determined based on experience, skills, education, geographic location, and alignment with our overall compensation structure.

Medical, dental, and vision insurance

The role

A lot of performance creative work goes into creating demand that wasn't there. That's not the problem here. Our customer already wants what we sell. Their heel hurts every morning when they get out of bed, or their ankle rolls on uneven ground and they've stopped trusting it.

What they don't believe is that this is the thing that finally works. They've already bought the insoles, done the stretches, and gone to physio twice. So you have to teach before you can sell, and you have to earn trust from someone who has been let down already. It's a harder brief than most, and a more interesting one.

You'll write our paid social advertising and own angle development and testing, reporting to our Creative Director. Expect to ship around 15 briefs a week, a mix of net-new concepts and iterations on ads that are already working. Your week is writing, research, and feedback to editors.

You don't need a physiotherapy background, but you do need to pick up a clinical concept quickly enough to explain it clearly and honestly in fifteen seconds of camera time.

What you'll do

  • Find new winning angles. Better creative is what lets us spend more, so we need a steady supply of ads that keep working as budgets grow.
  • Open new audiences. Runners, older adults worried about falling, people on their feet all day. Each group buys for a different reason, and every one we crack opens up new demand.
  • Get more life out of winners. Read the data weekly, iterate what's working, retire what's finished.
  • Write the scripts. Short and long-form video, hooks that stop the scroll, dialogue that sounds like a real person. This is most of your week.

  • Fast-growing company whose mission is to solve chronic pain and injuries
  • You’ll see the direct impact of your work on business results

The Role:

IonQ is building the world’s first fully-expressive, full-stack quantum computer based on trapped ion technology. Quantum computing is poised to reshape medicine, materials, simulation, and much more. To support our rapid growth, we’re hiring creative collaborators with top skills in their areas of expertise and a commitment to success.

We are looking for a Senior Account Executive - US Federal - Space Force that will be part of our US Federal Go-To-Market team whose mission is to bring IonQ’s offering—including Quantum Hardware (Systems and Networks), Software, Applications, and Access—to a curated set of clients across the US Department of War.   • Strategic Space, Land, and T&E Partnerships: Cultivate and maintain executive-level relationships within the U.S. Space Force (e.g., Space Systems Command, Space RCO), U.S. Army (e.g., AFC, PEO IEW&S, PEO STRI), and the Test Resource Management Center (TRMC). Navigate RDT&E accounts and transition technologies into Programs of Record (PoR), ensuring alignment with the Army’s 2030/2040 Transformation and the Space Force’s vision for a resilient space order of battle.
  • Full Lifecycle Capture Management: Own the end-to-end sales and capture lifecycle. This includes navigating the federal acquisition process, leading technical qualifications, and managing formal RFI/RFP responses. Execute complex negotiations for defense-specific vehicles, including OTAs, SBIR/STTR Phase II/III, and TRMC-specific funding streams (e.g., Central Test and Evaluation Investment Program).

Drive long-term adoption, facilitate contract renewals, and identify expansion opportunities for new mission sets across the Space and Land domains.

Requirements:

Every engagement feeds into our proprietary data infrastructure, enabling a continuous feedback loop that accelerates growth, improves margins, and compounds results across our client portfolio.

What began as a boutique design studio has evolved into one of the fastest-growing private companies in America (Inc. 5000) and among the most effective performance media agencies of the 2020s (Varos). Our founders were recognized by Forbes 30 Under 30 for advancing the intersection of technology, marketing, and advertising, cementing Darkroom’s role as a defining player in the future of media innovation.

About the role

We are looking for a deeply technical Senior Retention Specialist to own the CRM build for a high-growth consumer technology client. You will architect and implement the flows and automations that carry the program, own the segmentation logic behind them, and hold the channel KPIs that determine whether any of it lands in the inbox.

You are standing this program up from the ground, not inheriting it. The list starts near 20,000 and scales rapidly behind a significant acquisition investment — which puts real pressure on deliverability, list hygiene, and data hygiene from day one. Volume ramps to 40–60 emails a month, and increasingly granular segmentation is what generates that output. Automation is the core of the program: lead capture, welcome series, and the first-conversion funnel first, then subscription activation, loyalty, repeat purchase, and win-back. You will work in an enterprise-grade platform — Braze, Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Iterable, , or comparable.

You are the person who knows the platform better than anyone else on the team. When something does not fire, does not render, or does not deliver, you find out why.

You should apply if this sounds like you

You are hands-on in the ESP every day and you like it there. You enjoy building a journey with real conditional logic, and you get genuine satisfaction from tracking down why one segment stopped converting.

  • 3–5+ years of hands-on lifecycle, CRM, or email marketing execution, with deep expertise in at least one enterprise-grade ESP — Braze, Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Iterable, , or comparable.

  • You have built complex, event-triggered journeys from scratch: multi-branch logic, wait steps, conditional splits, holdouts, and cross-channel orchestration across email, SMS, push, and in-app.

  • You are fluent in advanced segmentation — behavioral and product-event based, computed attributes, dynamic and personalized content — and you have scaled a program where segmentation drove a real increase in send volume.

  • You have built the funnel that matters here: lead capture forms and opt-in logic, welcome series, first-conversion sequences, and subscription activation journeys.

  • You have implemented loyalty, rewards, and win-back programs, and you treat driving repeat purchase and long-term value as a core outcome rather than a nice-to-have.

  • You own deliverability as a discipline: domain warming and authentication (SPF, DKIM, DMARC, BIMI), sending reputation, list hygiene, sunset policies, and what to do when a list grows very fast.

  • You own the channel KPIs — open, click, click-to-open, conversion, deliverability, bounce, spam complaints, unsubscribe — and you can diagnose a drop in any of them.

  • You are comfortable with HTML and CSS for email, and you know how to build templates and modules that render correctly across clients. Liquid, Handlebars, AMPscript, or a similar templating language is a strong plus.

  • You understand data flows into the ESP: API-based events, webhooks, ETL or CDP integrations, and product event streams. You can hold a technical conversation with a client's engineering team.

  • You are a systematic troubleshooter — you isolate variables, you check the data before the theory, and you document what you find.

  • You design and execute proper tests: A/B and multivariate, with honest reads on significance.

  • Excellent written communication and the ability to explain a technical problem to a non-technical audience clearly and without condescension.

A day in the life

  • Build and QA the flows, automations, and campaigns that run your client's program — from lead capture and welcome through activation, loyalty, repeat purchase, and win-back.

We hold a high bar for performance, creativity, and ownership — but we also support each other relentlessly. No egos, no red tape — just world-class talent building something remarkable.

jobs.excerpt: Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous!
jobs.description:
Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous!

Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains.

Today, over 550 enterprise customers use BLP across 1,300+ deployed projects. In the processes we automate, customers achieve productivity improvements of 5 to 10 times.

To date, BLP remains majority employee-owned, with Goldman Sachs holding a minority stake as a growth investor. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies.

BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America.

Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard.

Location

This is a full-time position based at our HQ in central Zurich or in Munich.

About the role

You solve the hard technical problems on live systems.

Once a customer is running on blp, their processes are business critical. Invoices post or they do not. Orders flow or they sit. Our support organisation resolves most of what comes in, and a lot of it is genuinely well handled by people early in their career. What is left is yours: the cases where the cause is not obvious, where it crosses systems, data and process logic at once, where the same symptom has three possible explanations and only one of them is right.

That is the job. Not a queue, and not the easy half of one. Everything difficult that comes out of the run phase lands with you.

Two things sit alongside the case work, and they are what make this a senior job rather than a harder version of a junior one.

Stabilising accounts
When an account's health goes bad, you go in and stabilise it. Not as a permanent assignment, but as a small, highly skilled squad that takes a customer whose numbers or whose confidence have slipped, works out what is actually wrong across the whole picture, fixes it, and hands back a customer who is running properly again. It is the most concentrated version of this work there is.

Taking effort out permanently
Anything that keeps arriving in the queue is a signal, and the answer is usually not more people answering it. It might be better self-service for customers, a customer-facing assistant that resolves the routine questions before they reach us, better diagnostics, or a change in how something is configured at deployment so the problem never occurs. You are expected to find those, make the case, and drive them through. That is how a support organisation scales without scaling headcount one for one, and it is value the customer feels directly.

You work across the boundary between what our platform does, what the customer's ERP does, and what their data actually looks like. You are the one who can read a failing case end to end and say what really happened, and then say credibly whether the fix is configuration, data, process, or a genuine product issue. When it is a product issue, you are the counterpart to our engineering and product teams: you bring the evidence, and because you have seen the same structural problem across several customers, your case is the one that moves the roadmap.

You are also how this function gets better rather than just bigger. The diagnostic tooling, the patterns, the documentation that lets a first-year person resolve what used to take a senior one: that is yours to build. And the interns and specialists coming through the team learn this craft from you.

You do not deliver integrations and you do not run go-lives. Our integrations engineers and technical project managers own that. You own what happens once it is live and it is challenging.

What you'll do

  • Own the technically difficult cases from our live customer base, end to end, to a verified root cause.

  • Diagnose across boundaries: platform behaviour, ERP behaviour, master data and process logic.

  • Decide what the real fix is, and make it: configuration, data, process, or a case for engineering.

  • Go into accounts with a deteriorating health score, diagnose across the whole picture, stabilise them and hand them back running properly.

  • Drive strategic initiatives that permanently reduce effort and improve the customer experience, from better diagnostics to customer-facing self-service and assistants.

  • Act as the counterpart to Product and Engineering, with evidence strong enough to change priorities.

  • Recognise structural problems across customers and push for them to be solved once.

  • Build the diagnostic tooling, patterns and documentation that raise what the rest of the team can resolve alone.

  • Mentor interns and earlier-career colleagues, and raise the technical bar of the function.

  • Support Consultants and Customer Success Managers on the technical substance of customer escalations.

What we're really looking for

The following key attributes ensure success in this role:

  • Root Cause, Not Symptom – You are not finished when it stops happening. You are finished when you know why.

  • Cross-Boundary Reasoning – You hold platform, ERP, data and process in your head at once and find where the truth is.

  • Credible Both Ways – You explain the same problem to an engineer and to a CFO, and both of them believe you.

  • Leverage – Your instinct is to remove the next hundred cases, not only to close this one. You would rather build the thing that makes a problem stop arriving.

  • Calm Under Escalation – When a business-critical process is stopped, you get more precise rather than faster.

  • Stabilizer Under Pressure: An unhappy client is not a fire to put out. It is a relationship to rebuild. You bring the temperature down, put structure back into the account, and align next steps so trust returns, not just silence

What you'll bring

  • Master's degree in a STEM field: computer science, engineering, information systems, mathematics, physics or similar. Strong candidates from a related field are welcome to make their case.

  • 3+ years in a technical customer-facing role: application support at depth, technical consulting, solution engineering, integration engineering or equivalent.

  • Demonstrable debugging ability across systems, not only within one. APIs, data mapping, interfaces, logs.

  • Comfortable with data. SQL or equivalent, and the instinct to check rather than assume.

  • German and English, both fluent. This is a hard requirement. Our customers work in German every day and our internal work runs in English.

  • Nice to have: ERP experience with SAP, Microsoft Dynamics or similar, scripting in any language, or exposure to workflow automation and process mining.

What you'll get

  • The hard problems, not the queue.

  • Influence on the product, with a direct line to Engineering and Product.

  • Room to shape the function, since the practice is still being built.

  • Real growth – the path from here leads into Consulting, technical leadership within Customer Success, or Product.

  • Employee ownership – be part of a majority employee-owned company with a best-in-class stock option programme.

  • Amazing team – become part of a driven and collaborative group of innovators.

  • Visits & offsites – including collaborative team offsites.

Ready to build the future of ERP automation? Join us and own your impact.

jobs.description:
Overview

The HRU requires a remote Occupational Health Physician support to provide case review services of occupational medical exams performed for medical clearance, medical surveillance, reasonable accommodation, medical review board, and other purposes as needed by the DEA. This review is provided by a Reviewing Medical Officer (RMO) who makes a recommendation for clearance based on the medical information provided to make a medical recommendation to the DEA regarding an applicant or employee’s ability to perform their job duties safely.

Location: Remote for the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) located at 75 Morrissette Dr, Springfield, VA 22152

Pay: $140/hr

Schedule: Services shall be provided Monday - Friday between the hours of 0830 - 1700 EST. Averaging 40 hours each week

Position Type: Independent Contractor (1099)

Responsibilities

Perform duties of Reviewing Medical Officer (RMO) to make medical recommendations to DEA about a worker’s ability to perform their job duties safely by reviewing exams and associated medical documents within 30 days of receiving paperwork.

Communicate daily with DEA Health Services Unit staff to determine work priorities, issues encountered, and discuss individual exams as needed. RMO will communicate as needed to 3rd parties such as personal or treating physicians in order to successfully and accurately issue a clearance determination.

Provide weekly reports to the DEA on productivity.

Utilize federal, agency specific, and industry medical standards established prior to the examination to make a medical determination of fitness for duty.

Perform clearance case reviews; make a determination about whether the applicantor employee meets job specific medical standards to safely perform work that is arduous, involve a high degree of sensitivity toward the public or sensitive national security concerns, or put employees at risk of hazardous exposures during the course of performing essential job functions. The RMO determination shall address:

  • Whether the applicant or employee is medically cleared to work with or without
  • Whether the applicant or employee is medically able or unable to work.
  • Employee has a suspected work-related injury or illness.
  • Whether or not additional information is needed to make the medical
  • Whether to accelerate exam frequency and/or further evaluation such as additionalmedical testing or a Fitness for Duty evaluation is warranted.

Case reviews shall include examinations performed prior to employment for applicants, for periodic medical evaluation of incumbents, before return to work after an injury, or to determine an incumbent’s ongoing fitness for duty when a change in health status has caused concern about the worker’s or others’ safety.

When conducting medical screening and medical surveillance case reviews, the RMO determines whether there is a change in the health status of an employee due to apotential exposure at work. Requirements for these examinations fall under the general OSHA standard. The RMO determination will address:

  • Whether the health status of an employee has changed due to a potential workplace exposure.
  • Whether work areas require further evaluation due to medical information that raises suspicion for an unsafe work environment.

In determining medical support for medical employability case review, agency specific requests shall include:

  • Reasonable Accommodation under the Americans with Disabilities Act
  • Leave under the Family Medical Leave Act
  • Medical Fitness for Duty evaluations
  • Return to work after illness or injury
  • Handicapped parking requests
  • Federal disability retirement applications
  • Advanced sick leave and leave bank requests
  • Hardship requests

The RMO shall provide consultative occupational medical services related to agency and occupational health needs. The consultative services may include:

  • Subject Matter Expertise in Medical Review Board proceedings
  • Assistance with developing medical guidelines and standards
  • Creating agency policies and standard operating procedures for medical issues
  • Providing medical guidance on and evaluations for specific occupational medicine issues that arise in the workplace

In any instance, absence of specific guidance for medical determinations requires RMO research and expertise in collaboration with agency POC to develop consistent protocols for evaluation.

Transmission: Encrypted documents will be furnished electronically to RMO’s DEA email address, and will be returned via same. All communications should be via DEA email or shared folder.

The Contractor’s management organization shall be responsible for ensuring that all work activities are performed in a timely and cost-effective manner while maintaining the highest quality of performance. The Contractor shall: (1) prepare monthly status reports; and (2) participate in ad hoc status meetings. The Contractor shall ensure that project management activities are reflective of all active task orders.

Litigation Support. The Contractor’s reviewing physicians, specialists, or other staff may berequired to provide legal testimony or testify in court proceedings for the DEA. These services may include:

    • Providing copies of medical files and related documentation
    • Ad hoc consulting
    • Participate in investigatory interviews in person or by electronic means
    • Prepare affidavits
    • Participate in depositions by electronic means
    • Provide testimony by electronic means

Qualifications

  • Experience: Minimum 12 months specialized expertise and experience rendering opinions about whether an applicant or employee is medically qualified to perform the duties of their position, with or without accommodation.
  • Education: Completed Undergraduate Program and Medical School (MD/DO).Specialized training in Occupational Health Medicine.
  • Licensure: Unrestricted state licensure in state of practice
  • Certification: General Practitioner, at minimum; Contractor shall be a board-certified in Occupational Health Medicine or board-certified in Preventive Medicine
  • Malpractice Insurance: Provider is required to provide their own malpractice insurance.
  • Demonstrate the ability to convey expert medical opinions and advice using excellent communication skills. Communications will primarily be in writing. If needed, contractor shall be able to provide expert witness testimony related to case reviews performed.

With a corporate office in Honolulu, Hawaii and recruiting office in San Antonio, Texas we specialize in providing skilled, trained and highly successful healthcare workers, including RNs, CRNAs, Physicians, LPN/LVN, Licensed Social Workers, and many more.

We provide secure and isolated private networks, connectivity from cloud resources to internet and external networks, and networking services such as routing, security groups, load balancing and VPN connectivity.

Documentation & Administration

Coordination & Communication

Program Support

  • Ability to follow established processes and execute tasks accurately and on time

  • Strong, clear written and verbal communication skills
  • Familiarity with information security or compliance concepts

  • Reliable, methodical, and process-oriented
  • Willingness to learn and grow within a compliance function

THE FOLLOWING SKILLS ARE PREFERRED BUT NOT REQUIRED:

Work from or close to home:

With locations in Colorado and Massachusetts, OMH is continuing to expand into states around the country. OMH will work with you to identify the best “fit” and will provide everything you need to treat OMH patients remotely from the comfort of your home. Our interview process focuses on your skill sets, interest as well as geographic location to match you to the best available option to begin working with OMH. Ask to speak with our recruitment team today to identify the local office(s) in your area, as well as those offices that are being planned for launch. Of course, if you prefer to work from home, we also have fully remote positions available.

Responsibilities:

The Psychiatric Nurse Practitioner (PMHNP-BC) will participate in the integrated care team model at OMH. Outpatient behavioral health practices like OMH are getting more attention than ever before due to the emphasis on team approaches. Join OMH to perfect your skills in the emerging field of integrated behavioral health care. The interdisciplinary health care team includes physicians, psychiatric nurse practitioners, licensed clinical psychologists, and licensed mental health professionals (LCSW/LPC/LMFT/LMHC). OMH values clinical relationships between all provider levels and believes this coordinated, collaborative approach provides the highest level of care to the patients we are privileged to serve.

Customize the care for each patient:

Our clinicians have the unique ability to customize the care for each and every individual patient. You will have the autonomy to determine how often you see a patient as well as the appropriate length of time spent with each patient. Medication management and individual psychotherapy are the most common forms of clinical work performed at OMH, but our clinicians also perform family therapy, group therapy, and psychological testing as needed and/or appropriate to a wide range of presenting problems of our patients.

Pick your own schedule!

  • Enjoy the freedom to create your own custom schedules with the perfect work/life balance.
  • Typically, clinicians work between Mondays – Fridays somewhere between the hours of 7:00 AM – 7:00 PM.

Focus on the patient’s care without the hassle or any additional on-call responsibilities. Simply cover the care for you own patients! Our medical staff and clinical psychotherapists focus on the patient’s care and our back-office support team handles the rest. This allows our clinicians time to be spent where it should be; with the patients they serve. Each clinician is responsible for clinical care and documentation following treatment sessions. Once that’s complete, our support team will handle all billing, collections, credentialing, etc. Once you leave the office for the day, your time is yours. No additional on-call responsibilities and no time spent wasted dealing with insurance companies.

Interested in benefits?

Full-time clinicians are eligible for medical health benefits. Please speak with the recruitment team to obtain additional specifics on benefits.

Leadership & Advancement:

OMH is a growing, clinician-led company. Our Site Supervisors are geographically dispersed throughout the areas we work in order to have staff leaders available to every clinician. Talk with our recruitment team today about the advancement opportunities to become senior psychotherapists and/or site supervisors.

Licensure, Education & Experience:                                    

Licensure in Colorado and/or Massachusetts as a Psychiatric Nurse Practitioner with experience working with persons who have various behavioral health issues such as, mood disorders, anxiety disorders, personality disorders, substance misuse, and other psychiatric impairments under the supervision of a consulting psychiatrist(s).  We welcome new graduates!

Preferred: Successful completion of PMHNP-BC exam(s).

This document represents the major duties, responsibilities, and authorities of this job, and is not intended to be a complete list of all tasks and functions. Other duties may be assigned as well.

jobs.title: Senior QA Engineer (Full-Stack, Automation-Heavy)
jobs.excerpt: Why Altium Software Engineering? Renesas 365 (R365) is a new cloud platform for electronics system design, combining hardware and software workflows.
jobs.description:
Why Altium Software Engineering?

Renesas 365 (R365) is a new cloud platform for electronics system design, combining hardware and software workflows. The domain involves complex data relationships and system-level interactions.

Altium offers the opportunity to conceive and build new product features for electronics engineers, and add your own ideas to the world’s most collaborative and efficient electronics design platform.

About the Role

This is a full-stack QA role focused on test automation and feature coverage.
Please note: This is not an AQA (Automation QA) role — test frameworks are maintained by a dedicated AQA team.

A Day in the Life of Our Senior QA Engineer

  • Own feature quality end-to-end (UI + API)
  • Write automated tests using existing tools:
  • Selenium WebDriver
  • Reqnroll (BDD)
  • Playwright (growing direction)
  • Ensure full test coverage of features
  • Maintain and extend automated scenarios
  • Participate in regression and release testing
  • Work with CI pipelines (run/debug tests)
  • Collaborate with AQA team on framework usage

What We’re Looking For

  • 4+ years of experience as a QA Engineer
  • Experience in automated testing using existing frameworks
  • Ability to write and understand test code (C# is preferrable)
  • Experience testing web applications (UI + API)
  • Understanding of test design and coverage
  • Experience with CI/CD and Git

Nice to have

  • Experience with Playwright
  • Experience with GraphQL APIs

jobs.title: AI Researcher — AI Architecture Research
jobs.excerpt: About the RoleWe’re looking for an AI Researcher focused on AI architecture research to help design, analyze, and advance next-generation model architectures.
jobs.description:
About the Role

We’re looking for an AI Researcher focused on AI architecture research to help design, analyze, and advance next-generation model architectures. You’ll work at the intersection of theory and production—publishing novel research while collaborating closely with engineers to turn ideas into real systems.

This role is ideal for someone who has published research papers and wants to see their work directly shape deployed models, not just benchmarks.

What You’ll Work On

  • Research and design novel AI architectures (e.g. alternatives to standard Transformer designs, long-context models, efficient sequence modeling, hybrid architectures)

  • Explore architectural improvements for scalability, efficiency, and stability

  • Prototype and evaluate new architectures through ablations, benchmarks, and empirical studies

  • Author and co-author research papers for top ML conferences and journals

  • Collaborate with engineering teams to translate research into training and inference systems

  • Stay current with state-of-the-art research and identify promising directions early

What We’re Looking For

  • Strong background in machine learning research, with a focus on model architecture

  • Publication record in ML/AI venues (e.g. NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, COLM, ACL, EMNLP, arXiv)

  • Deep understanding of:

    • Neural network architectures

    • Sequence models and attention mechanisms

    • Training dynamics and optimization

  • Hands-on experience with PyTorch or JAX

  • Ability to reason rigorously, design clean experiments, and communicate results clearly

  • Comfortable working in a fast-moving startup environment

Nice to Have

  • Experience with non-Transformer architectures (e.g. RNN-based, state-space, hybrid models)

  • Work on long-context or memory-efficient models

  • Open-source research contributions

  • Experience bridging research and production systems

  • Background in efficient training or inference-aware architecture design

Why Join Us

  • High ownership over research direction and roadmap

  • Clear path to publishing impactful work

  • Tight feedback loop between research and real-world deployment

  • Small, highly technical team with strong research culture

  • Competitive compensation and meaningful equity
